text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER - prod-gpu-usw2: GPU node queue length >= 1200, sustained 3m. Autoscaler failing to provision GPU nodegroups. Paging oncall. Incident ID=INC-20260315-09
ryan_oncall: Acked. I’m on it. Any early customer impact notes? :pager:
cs-ellie: We’ve got 3 customers reporting timeouts for inference endpoints in us-west-2. Ticket IDs #4123, #4124, #4127. CS is triaging SLA risk.
maya_sre: Quick dump from the autoscaler logs — it repeatedly tries to create instances but API returns launch template / iam errors. Pasting excerpts:
```
2026-03-15T09:02:43Z autoscaler: Instance creation failed: InvalidLaunchTemplateVersion: LaunchTemplate version 7 does not exist for lt-0abcd
2026-03-15T09:03:11Z autoscaler: AttachRole failed: AccessDenied: iam:PassRole
2026-03-15T09:03:11Z autoscaler: Node group tainting omitted due to template mismatch
```
omar_runtime: Also seeing backlog in request queue on the runtime side; `/metrics/gpu_queue_length` shows spike and continuous growth, batching can't clear. We have token throttling kicking in on storefront.
lina_infra: I’m checking ASG and LT history. There was an automated LT rollout 30m before pager. New versions were published but not all nodegroups were updated; some ASGs still reference older version IDs and the autoscaler picks latest by tag causing mismatch.
ryan_oncall: Can we manually scale up a fallback nodegroup that still has a healthy launch template version? If we can get a few nodes up we can drain the backlog.
lina_infra: I can manual increment desired capacity on the legacy GPU-ASG (gpu-pool-legacy) to +4 nodes. But note the old LT uses a different instance profile — I’ll validate IAM passrole perms first.
maya_sre: Meanwhile, we should reduce load to prevent queue growth. Omar, can runtime shed non-critical batch jobs?
omar_runtime: Yes — enabling `runtime.feature.batch_backpressure` to true and lowering max_batch_size from 256 -> 64; applying now. This will reduce throughput but buy time.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook step 2: If autoscaler error contains "AccessDenied: iam:PassRole", run `aws iam get-role --role-name <node-role>` and check `iam:PassRole` trust. If missing, escalate to infra.
ryan_oncall: Lina — status on manual scale and IAM check?
lina_infra: IAM role has PassRole on the new LT role missing for the autoscaler service principal. I can attach `iam:PassRole` to the autoscaler role temporarily (least-priv), then retry create. Patch applied.
maya_sre: After IAM fix, autoscaler attempts succeed but nodes are coming up with incorrect taint keys, kubelet rejects because the K8s version label doesn't match cluster autoscaler expectations. Excerpt:
```
kubelet[1234]: node "ip-10-0-12-34" tainted with key "gpu.redwood.io/taint" value "experimental" but cluster expects "gpu.redwood.io/pool"
```
omar_runtime: That explains node registration failures — autoscaler spins but kube rejects and they get cordoned.
ryan_oncall: Two parallel actions: Lina to patch launch template tags/labels to match expected taints and Maya to restart cluster-autoscaler with logs verbose. Omar keep shedding non-essential traffic. I’ll coordinate customer comms.
lina_infra: I’m rolling a quick LT patch to set `UserData` tag env var: `REDFOX_TAINT_POOL=prod-gpu` and bumping LT version to v8. Updating ASG to point at v8 for gpu-pool-legacy. Doing one zone at a time.
maya_sre: Restarted cluster-autoscaler with debug flags `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false --scale-down-unneeded-time 10m` and tailing logs. Now seeing successful joins: `Registered node ip-10-0-12-34 as pool prod-gpu`
ops-runbook-bot: Step 6 complete: Run `kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=prod-gpu` to confirm nodes Ready.
omar_runtime: New nodes are registering and starting workers, queue drain started — queue length plateaued at ~980 then dropped to 400 over 7m. Throttling cleared for highest priority customers.
cs-ellie: Notifying impacted customers that mitigation is in progress; CS message sent with ETA 15-30m.
ryan_oncall: Good. Root cause summary draft: launch template rollout left mixed versions and new LT lacked expected taint metadata and autoscaler IAM passrole perms. Cascade: autoscaler retries -> failed instances -> node registration mismatch -> queue growth -> customer timeouts.
maya_sre: Postmortem action items (initial):
- enforce LT version gating in CI + canary rollout policy
- autoscaler should validate LT metadata before create attempt
- add synthetic probe for `iam:PassRole` during nodegroup reconcile
- add per-customer SLA routing to degrade batch to dedicated pools first
ryan_oncall: I’ll open INC-20260315 and assign owners. Lina, Maya, Omar please add follow-ups to respective squads.
lina_infra: Will roll back the unintended LT auto-rollout system and add a preflight check.
omar_runtime: I’ll add runtime backpressure defaults and a safer batch cutoff for priority queues.
cs-ellie: CS will follow up with impacted customers with post-incident notes and credits as needed.
ryan_oncall: Incident moving to CONTAINED. Will mark as MONITORING. Please keep updates in this thread until we close. :thumbsup:
